card.name: Sevillanas
card.tagline: Seville — flamenco's polite cousin. Every Andalusian wedding ends with it.
card.profile: Sevillanas (Spanish pronunciation: [seβiˈʝanas]) are a type of folk music and dance of Sevilla and its region. They were derived from the Seguidilla, an old Castilian folk music and dance genre. In the nineteenth century they were influenced by Flamenco. They have a relatively limited musical pattern but are rich in lyrics based on country life, virgins, country towns, neighborhoods, pilgrimage, and love themes. Sevillanas can be heard mainly in fairs and festivals, including the famous Seville Fair (Feria de abril de Sevilla).
card.insight: Sevillanas is danced at every April Feria de Sevilla (begun 1847) by an estimated 500,000 attendees over six days; the four-coplas structure was codified by composer Manuel Pareja-Obregón in the 1950s.
